extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and instructors learning algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory chapter material defining paths, homotopy, loops and the fundamental group; basic constructions (product, reparametrization), covering spaces and lifting, computation π1(S1) ≈ Z, and several standard applications (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, Brouwer, Borsuk–Ulam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Path (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path in a space X is a continuous map f: I → X where I = [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to model motion from a starting point f(0) to an endpoint f(1). Paths are the basic objects whose deformations are studied; later specialized to loops when endpoints coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy of paths (endpoints fixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: A homotopy of paths in X is a family f_t : I → X, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, such that (1) endpoints f_t(0) and f_t(1) are independent of t; (2) the associated map F: I × I → X given by F(s,t)=f_t(s) is continuous. When f_0 and f_1 are connected this way we write f_0 ≃ f_1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes continuously deforming a path while keeping endpoints fixed. Example: linear homotopies in R^n via f_t(s)=(1−t)f_0(s)+t f_1(s). Homotopy is shown to be an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop and basepoint; definition of π1(X,x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: A loop is a path f: I → X with f(0)=f(1)=x0 (basepoint). The set of homotopy classes [f] of loops at x0 is denoted π1(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loops are the elements of the fundamental group. All intermediate loops during homotopies must also start and end at the basepoint. Notation: when X is path-connected the dependence on basepoint is up to isomorphism and often suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product (composition) of paths and well-definedness on homotopy classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Given paths f,g with f(1)=g(0) the product f * g is the path traversing f then g, defined by f*g(s)=f(2s) for 0≤s≤1/2 and g(2s−1) for 1/2≤s≤1. If f_0 ≃ f_1 and g_0 ≃ g_1 then f_0*g_0 ≃ f_1*g_1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines concatenation of motions and ensures the product descends to homotopy classes, enabling group operations on π1. Reparametrization (precomposing with continuous ϕ:I→I with ϕ(0)=0,ϕ(1)=1) preserves homotopy classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: π1(X,x0) is a group (identity, associativity, inverses)
rubrics_metrics.description: With product [f][g]=[f*g], π1(X,x0) is a group: associative (up to homotopy, shown via explicit reparametrization), identity is the class of the constant path at x0, and inverses are homotopy classes of reversed paths f̄(s)=f(1−s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses reparametrizations to show associativity and constant/reparametrized paths to show identities; explicit homotopies demonstrate inverses. Emphasizes working with homotopy classes, not individual parametrizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparametrization preserves homotopy class
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ: I→I is continuous with ϕ(0)=0 and ϕ(1)=1 then f◦ϕ ≃ f via a homotopy of reparametrizations ϕ_t(s)=(1−t)ϕ(s)+t s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows one to change speed or timing of traversing a path without changing its homotopy class — important in associativity and product constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change-of-basepoint isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If h:I→X is a path from x0 to x1 then β_h: π1(X,x1)→π1(X,x0) defined by β_h([f])=[h * f * h̄] is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So for path-connected X the isomorphism class of π1(X,x0) is independent of basepoint. Proof: β_h is a homomorphism with inverse β_{h̄} and uses concatenation properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simply-connected criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X is simply-connected iff it is path-connected and π1(X) is trivial (i.e., there is a unique homotopy class of paths connecting any two points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence proved by relating uniqueness of connecting paths to triviality of loops; used as a characterization of simply-connectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of covering space and 'evenly covered' condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering space of X is a space X̃ and a map p:X̃→X such that for each x∈X there is an open neighborhood U with p^{-1}(U) a disjoint union of open sets each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p. Such U is called evenly covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: p:R→S^1 given by p(s)=(cos 2π s, sin 2π s) where any open arc in S^1 is evenly covered. This property underlies path-lifting and homotopy-lifting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path-lifting and homotopy-lifting properties (a),(b),(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For each path f:I→X starting at x0 and each x̃0∈p^{-1}(x0) there is a unique lift f̃ of f starting at x̃0. (b) For each homotopy f_t : I→X of paths starting at x0 and each lift of f_0 starting at x̃0, there is a unique lifted homotopy f̃_t of paths starting at x̃0. (c) More generally: given F:Y×I→X and a lift F̃|_{Y×{0}}, there is a unique lift F̃:Y×I→X̃ restricting to the given lift on Y×{0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial tools used in the proof that π1(S^1) ≈ Z and in many other arguments; existence and uniqueness obtained by working over evenly covered neighborhoods and compactness/induction on subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation: π1(S^1) ≈ Z (Theorem 1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: π1(S^1) is an infinite cyclic group generated by the homotopy class of the loop ω(s)=(cos 2π s, sin 2π s) based at (1,0). Every loop is homotopic to ω^n for a unique integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the covering map p:R→S^1, lifts of loops to paths in R, and uniqueness of endpoint to determine an integer winding number. Strategy generalizes via covering-space lifting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra via π1(S^1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complex polynomial p(z) has no root, one constructs loops f_r(s)=p(r e^{2π i s})/|p(r e^{2π i s})| in S^1 and shows they are nullhomotopic for all r; comparing with a large r where f_r homotopes to ω^n yields a contradiction unless degree n=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates how algebraic facts can follow from topological invariants (winding number / degree); typical argument is by contradiction using homotopies of loops and theorem π1(S^1)=Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Brouwer fixed point theorem (2D) via nonexistence of retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: If h:D^2→D^2 had no fixed point one can define a continuous retraction r:D^2→S^1; but any loop in S^1 is nullhomotopic in D^2, so composing with r would give a nullhomotopy in S^1 contradicting π1(S^1)≠0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how fundamental group obstructions rule out certain maps (retractions), giving existence results (fixed points) by contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Borsuk–Ulam theorem (n=2) via lifting parity argument
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuous f:S^2→R^2, if no antipodal pair maps equal then g(x)=(f(x)−f(−x))/|f(x)−f(−x)| defines g:S^2→S^1. Composing with the equator loop and lifting yields an odd integer winding, contradicting nullhomotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses lift properties and parity argument of lifts to show existence of antipodal pair x,−x with f(x)=f(−x). Illustrates higher-topological consequences of π1 computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product spaces: π1(X×Y) ≈ π1(X) × π1(Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are path-connected then π1(X×Y) is isomorphic to π1(X)×π1(Y); loops and homotopies in the product correspond to pairs of loops and homotopies in the factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute π1 of tori (S^1×S^1 gives Z×Z) and higher-dimensional products by induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for decomposing loops via path-connected open cover (Lemma 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is union of path-connected open sets A_α each containing basepoint x0 and each intersection A_α∩A_β is path-connected, then every loop at x0 is homotopic to a product of loops each lying in a single A_α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses partitioning I into subintervals mapping into single A_α and inserting connecting paths in intersections; key technical lemma used to prove π1(S^n)=0 for n≥2 by covering sphere with two R^n-like sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of π1 for higher spheres (π1(S^n)=0 for n≥2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: write S^n as union of two open sets each homeomorphic to R^n with path-connected intersection S^{n−1}×R (for n≥2). Apply Lemma 1.15 and triviality of π1 on R^n to deduce all loops nullhomotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphisms and functoriality
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous map φ:(X,x0)→(Y,y0) induces φ_*:π1(X,x0)→π1(Y,y0) by [f]↦[φ∘f]. Properties: (φψ)_* = φ_* ψ_* and id_* = id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induced maps preserve products and homotopies; homeomorphisms induce isomorphisms on π1. This functoriality underlies many algebraic-topological comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and deformation retract implications for π1
rubrics_metrics.description: If X retracts onto A then inclusion i_*:π1(A,x0)→π1(X,x0) is injective. If A is a deformation retract of X then i_* is an isomorphism (both injective and surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use induced maps from the retraction r, since r∘i = id implies r_* i_* = id on π1(A). Used to deduce impossibility of S^1 retracting from D^2 and similar obstructions.
